claims.text: The investigated system is a single-crystal FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a single-crystal Cu matrix.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating initially has an FCC structure.
The coating initially has a low dislocation density.
Nanoindentation is performed to a depth of 30 Å at 10 m/s and at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K.
Dislocation density decreases at 600 K relative to 300 K.
The decrease in dislocation density at 600 K increases the elastic modulus.
Rapid lattice disorder at higher temperatures correlates with sharp reductions in hardness and wear resistance.
Above 900 K, stacking faults are rapidly annihilated.
Stacking-fault annihilation reduces barriers to dislocation motion.
Enhanced dislocation climb and cross-slip above 900 K cause dislocation starvation.
Localized amorphization begins at the contact interface above 900 K.
Localized amorphization causes a transition from dislocation-mediated plasticity to viscous-like flow.
The proposed stacking-fault annihilation, dislocation-starvation, and amorphization cascade causes the friction-coefficient spike and loss of wear resistance above 900 K.
Thermal softening overwhelms mechanical annealing above 900 K.
Below 900 K, dislocation-mediated plasticity dominates and friction remains moderate.
The threshold for amorphization can vary with the interatomic potential, local stress state, and strain rate.
If disorder-driven thermal softening is primary, the HCP atom fraction will increase significantly above 900 K.
If disorder-driven thermal softening is primary, total dislocation line length will decrease sharply above 900 K because of annihilation.
If mechanical annealing dominates, the HCP atom fraction will remain low.
If mechanical annealing dominates, dislocation line length will change minimally.

contradictions.description: The proposed sequence starts with rapid stacking-fault annihilation, which would ordinarily reduce the population of HCP-classified stacking-fault atoms, but the falsification criterion predicts that the disorder-driven mechanism will produce a significant increase in HCP atom fraction. The hypothesis does not explain how these opposing signatures coexist.

Localized amorphization is treated as the decisive disorder event, yet the proposed test uses increasing HCP atom count as its positive signature. HCP ordering and amorphous/noncrystalline ordering are distinct structural classifications, so HCP counting alone is not a direct or internally coherent measure of amorphization onset.
